title: Assimilate: Strategy Sprint Retrospective
summary: Town-hall style sprint retrospective that covers Q2 strategy alignment, headcount asks, risk posture for Dedicated and Private launches, and a short demo of new console telemetry. Meeting included candid discussion of tradeoffs (latency vs cost), hiring priorities, and a recap of org-level OKRs.
topics: Risk review for Dedicated & Private launches
next_steps: Marco to circulate telemetry deck + sample dashboards by Fri 2026-04-24
People to run priority-hire intake with managers next week
Ops to run fire-drill on Dedicated region failover 2026-05-05
Product to finalize pilot criteria for Private by 2026-05-01
action_items: Marco Li - Share console telemetry deck and link to telemetry-demo recording - 2026-04-24
Jill Robertson - Collect priority hiring requests and publish intake doc - 2026-04-29
Rhea Patel - Schedule Dedicated region failover fire-drill and invite SRE leads - 2026-05-05
Devon Park - Publish pilot success criteria for Private deployment (security & latency thresholds) - 2026-05-01
Omar Singh - Prepare budget sensitivity for headcount scenarios Q2/Q3 - 2026-04-30
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-22 10:00 PDT | Duration: ~75 minutes | Location: All-hands Zoom | Recording id ff-2026-04-22-asm-001

[00:00] Asha Menon: okay, hey everyone thanks for joining, uh let's kick off, this is the Assimilate sprint retrospective, we'll go through the strategy anchors for Q2 then head into the telemetry demo, and leave time for Q&A. we're tryin' to be tight, uh about 75 minutes.

[00:20] Marco Li: quick note — the telemetry deck lives in drive under /product/telemetry/console-q2, i'll share the link in chat afterwards. i've got about 12 slides and a very short live demo.

[00:30] Speaker 3: (murmur) thanks Marco.

[00:45] Asha Menon: first up, big picture: the thesis hasn't changed — we're a serving company, right. it's about predictable inference economics, and we need to show that across hosted, dedicated and private. so priorities for the quarter: one, ship the Dedicated SLA and failover playbooks; two, stabilize Private onboarding velocity; three, reduce per-token cost by instrumentation-led batching and cache improvements.

[01:10] Devon Park: i want to call out the product ask — customers keep asking for more transparent cost breakdowns per token per model variant. we think a per-route cost heatmap will help sales and customers evaluate tradeoffs.

[01:36] Omar Singh: from finance POV, a per-route heatmap is useful but we need to understand margin delta for Dedicated contracts versus hosted. also headcount sensitivity — if we add three infra hires this quarter what's the runway impact.

[01:58] Jill Robertson: quick HR context: hiring velocity is…mixed. we've got strong offers out but ramp is still 8-12 weeks. hiring pipeline for SWE infra is solid but interview capacity is our bottleneck. i'll propose a reprioritized intake to focus on the top 5 roles.

[02:20] Asha Menon: let's mark that as an action — Jill to publish intake. (pauses) okay — onto risk posture for Dedicated and Private. Rhea?

[02:36] Rhea Patel: yep — our biggest operational risk is region failover for Dedicated customers. the orchestration layer is good but we have some k8s operator gaps in stateful failover of KV cache across regions; during last sim the KV cache, sorry, the KV cash, um, the KV cache, had partial miss rates and we saw latency spikes. we've got mitigation work but recommend we run a full fire-drill with customer-facing runbook. also we need stronger observability for cold starts on Private installs — those are the pain points.

[03:10] Marco Li: to add, the kernel/compilation heuristics are causing variability for long-seq tokens on some models, we have a tuning pass but we need to bake that into our canary rollout.

[03:28] Attendee: (someone) are we tracking performance regressions per model in the console? like automated alerts when per-token latency crosses a threshold?

[03:38] Marco Li: yes, that's part of the telemetry demo — threshold alerts, per-model perf histograms, and token-cost traces. but there are limits to retention and cost for high-resolution traces, so we'll show sampling config.

[04:05] Asha Menon: alright Marco let's roll the demo, but remember live demos can be flaky.

[04:20] Marco Li: launching the console — okay, i'm sharing my screen. you should see the dashboard with per-route latency, token cost, and a red alert on a canary model. this used to be called Redwood Console v2 — some of the names in transcripts may be garbage, sorry if the auto-caption does weird things.

[04:45] Marco Li: here's a latency percentile chart — p50, p95, p99 with a hover that shows the distribution by model variant. down here is a batching util panel which shows how auto-batching is grouping requests; we can change the batch window live. watch what happens when i expand burst window from 50ms to 200ms, cost drops but p99 climbs.

[05:20] Jill Robertson: (interject) can we surface suggested config? last time AE's spent a lot of cycles recommending thresholds — is there an auto-suggest?

[05:30] Marco Li: yes — optimize engine suggests profiles based on observed seq length distribution. it's heuristic right now — we'll tighten it with more workloads.

[05:45] Speaker 2: the demo looks good but the per-route cost numbers are sometimes off compared to billing; are they reconciled?

[05:55] Omar Singh: good question — we currently show estimated unit cost in the console; final billing runs through the billing pipeline which applies reserved capacity discounts etc. we should label estimates clearly.

[06:10] Asha Menon: move on to customer signals — Dev, what are we hearing?

[06:18] Devon Park: big theme: customers choosing Dedicated for predictable latency but being wary of lock-in and data residency. Private pilots are being requested by finance teams at enterprise accounts. also, sales flagged a competitor quoting aggressive pricing on embeddings and low-latency guarantees — likely a headfake, but we should be aware.

[06:45] Attendee: which competitor was that?

[06:47] Devon Park: heard OpenAI in one case, and some customers mentioned Vertex AI comparisons.

[06:55] Asha Menon: okay — competitive signals captured. now hiring: Jill, run us through the top 5 hires.

[07:03] Jill Robertson: prioritized list: two infra SREs (region failover), one backend infra engineer (kernel/compilation focus), one product analytics engineer (telemetry), one solutions engineer for Private deployments. i've got drafts of job briefs, will route links after this call. we also discussed contracting some bench interviewers to speed cycle.

[07:25] Marco Li: a note on the kernel engineering hire — that person needs low-level GPU/attention expertise and should be comfortable reading transformer kernels. hiring market is tight there.

[07:42] Rhea Patel: operations need triage capacity as well — adding two SREs will give us more runway on shift coverage for Dedicated and Private.

[08:00] Asha Menon: moving to finance — Omar?

[08:06] Omar Singh: high level: Q2 burn plan scenarios included in the pg deck. headcount add increases burn by ~8-10% depending on comp mix. Dedicated sales are slightly ahead of plan but revenue timing is variable — some customers want quarterly invoicing which delays recognition. i'll work with sales on bumping up conversion playbooks.

[08:30] Audience question: is SOC 2 renewal on track?

[08:34] Rhea Patel: yes we're on track, audit window scheduled for June; Private deployment audit checklist being updated — KMS integrations and audit log retention are the two big items.

[08:50] Asha Menon: okay — open Q&A time, please keep it short and practical.

[09:00] Attendee: are we prioritizing any specific region expansions? APAC demand increasing.

[09:06] Marco Li: APAC is next region for Dedicated; capacity is queued but we need to validate GPU families for latency SLOs. also we need to test routing policies across regions to avoid cold-start latencies.

[09:26] Attendee 5: can we get a short doc that maps which teams own which telemetry alerts? it's hard to know who responds when something triggers.

[09:34] Marco Li: noted — Marco + Rhea will publish a runbook that maps alerts to on-call groups.

[09:40] Asha Menon: let's talk briefly about the pilot criteria for Private. Devon?

[09:45] Devon Park: pilot criteria: security checklist complete (SSO, KMS), performance within 10% of hosted baseline for p95, and onboarding time under 6 weeks. if any of these fail, pilot doesn't graduate. we'll share a template for pilots.

[10:05] Attendee: what's the escape hatch if a Private pilot causes data residency requirement mismatches?

[10:10] Rhea Patel: we need clear T&Cs and an escalation path — legal and security will handle exceptions per-case.

[10:20] Asha Menon: as we head to a close, quick recap — action owners listed in the doc. please treat the intake and pilot criteria as high priority. any final lightning comments?

[10:40] Marco Li: will share the telemetry recording and raw metrics export. we'll also include a small spreadsheet showing cost vs latency tradeoffs for a few sample workloads.

[10:55] Jill Robertson: will run the intake workshop next Tuesday; invites will go out end of day.

[11:05] Omar Singh: i'll share budget scenarios and a short note on contract terms that impact revenue recognition.

[11:15] Asha Menon: thank you all — meeting adjourned. please review the action items and mark any dependencies in the intake doc.

[11:30] End of recording.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-caption had trouble with some technical nouns (KV cache -> KV cash, kernel optimizations -> kernel opti-miss, Redwood Console branding sometimes munged). There was occasional crosstalk during Q&A. The transcript has been lightly edited for readability but retains filler and false starts.
